title: A Double-Blinded Polysaccharide Analysis of 10 Products Labelled as Containing Mushrooms for Pets Purchased Online
content: Ten commercial mushroom products, sourced from resellers and labelled for veterinary use, were subjected to simple quantitative and qualitative polysaccharide analysis methods to differentiate products containing only mushrooms (the fruiting bodies of the fungal life-cycle) from those that include the whole solid fermentation resulting from the fungal mycelium of cereal grain. The therapeutic benefits of fungi are often attributed to their β-glucan content, which, unlike cereal grain β glucans, is uniquely characterized by 1,3-1,6 β glycosidic linkages. Fungal polysaccharide markers were used to distinguish mushroom-containing products from grain-based mycelial products in this study, which highlighted the compositional variability in marketplace products. Ten products labelled for pet use, and one for human use, were subjected to a multifaceted analytical approach by enzymatic quantification of α- and β-glucans and starch, and Lugol’s iodine staining for starch detection. The resulting analyses identified two distinct product profiles: 1) polysaccharide profiles consistent with mushrooms, exhibiting high β-glucan and low α-glucan content and 2) products consistent with fermentation of cereal grains by fungal mycelium that have lower levels of β-glucans, higher levels of α-glucans, and a strong positive iodine-starch test. This study provides objective, evidence-based criteria for differentiation of these product profiles; some products labelled as mushroom-derived contained predominantly grain. This method can be adapted to assess other fungal-derived products and verify the authenticity of mushroom-based veterinary products.
